name: Use the canonical catalog language from the context documents
description: The domain terms live in CONTEXT-MAP.md (the contexts and how they relate) and docs/contexts/<context>/CONTEXT.md (one glossary per context). Catalog and Inventory are written; others are added when their first seed starts. Use these terms exactly in code, docs and the UI, and check the glossary before adding a term. Keep the files current with the domain-modeling skill (~/.agents/skills/domain-modeling): a CONTEXT.md is only a glossary, with 1–2 sentence definitions and an Avoid list. docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md was never committed and is unavailable.

title: Save every change to part details as a new, complete revision
rationale: Each change to part details saves a new, complete revision that never changes afterwards, grouped in a Change with a reason. Commands carry the current revision they expect. Restoring adds a new revision, and a change that alters nothing is rejected. Superseded by mx-5e5fb1: since kicad-parts-7556 a details change saves new part details and adds no revision, only a CAD change adds one; Restore was removed in kicad-parts-9296. Supplier data, stock, scans and drafts never create revisions.

title: Keep a CAD item's identity, its stored bytes and its revisions separate
rationale: A CAD item keeps its identity over time. Its stored bytes are identified by their SHA-256, and each revision's hash covers its content and license. Source and license belong to one exact CAD item revision. Moving or copying stored bytes never creates a revision.

title: Keep verification and protection separate
rationale: Verification is permanent proof about one exact revision. Protection is an audited setting that blocks changes to a part or CAD item. To fix a protected item, remove the protection with a reason, revise it, verify the new revision, then protect it again. Authority is never a silent way around protection.

name: Binary-safe content addressing inside PocketBase hooks
description: $security.sha256 hashes text, so bytes that are not UTF-8 would hash wrongly. The CSV import sends blobs as base64 in the JSON command and infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_lib.js decodes and hashes them in pure JS before $filesystem.fileFromBytes, so blobs are checked and written in the same transaction; tooling/catalog-import test the_route_hashes_blob_bytes_exactly checks it against Rust's sha2 at 1, 55, 56, 63, 64, 119, 120 and 300,000 bytes (PocketBase cannot store an empty file, so the route refuses empty blobs, and it refuses a blob that no CAD item revision in the request uses). Canonical documents whose SHA-256 is their identity (revision snapshots) are stored in text fields with an explicit max (a TextField max of 0 means 5000), never json fields, so the hashed bytes round-trip. Shared hook code lives in a non-.pb.js file loaded with require(`${__hooks}/catalog_lib.js`) inside the handler.

title: Derive Catalog record IDs from content and compare CSV imports with stored state on the server
rationale: Every Catalog record ID is the first 15 hex digits of SHA-256('kicad-parts:<kind>:v1\n<key>') (part from IPN, CAD item from kind + LIB:NAME, CAD item revision from CAD item + revision number (since kicad-parts-54d5; see the pattern 'CAD item revisions are numbered; snapshots name them by number and hash'), blob from its bytes' hash, Change and audit entry from the correlation ID), computed in crates/catalog/src/ids.rs and re-derived by the route, so re-imports find the same records without a mapping table; a stored record is reused only if its hash or key matches, otherwise 409 id_collision. A symbol's blob is the exact bytes of that one top-level symbol (its source keeps file path, file hash and byte range), so editing a neighbouring symbol does not revise it; footprints and 3D models are whole files. Manufacturer parts (main first) are part details, so adding, removing or reordering one saves new part details (no revision, since kicad-parts-7556); a part has one datasheet, and a substitutes.csv datasheet that is neither blank nor the part's is a substitutes-csv-datasheet-differs import problem. POST /api/catalog/csv-imports compares with stored state in one transaction, and a Change is made only when there is at least one new revision or saved part details. Which import changes are saved and which become import problems is in the pattern 'Part details are stored apart from part revisions'. Supplier part numbers, LCSC codes and prices stay in the source, never in part details or a revision. Replaced in part: when a run is recorded without a Change and when an import is a 422 noop are now in mx-c5e787; expected revisions and the checkout check are in mx-64c42a.

name: Catalog write guards and tamper tests
description: catalog_write_guards.pb.js refuses every create, update and delete of catalog_* records through the record API with 403, superusers included (onRecord*Request hooks), and every update or delete from server code (onRecordUpdate/onRecordDelete) except moving a part's current_details to the details saved right after them (same part, number+1, predecessor = old current) and its current_revision to its newest revision that is not archived, computed in the hook from the transaction's records (since kicad-parts-5bea; archive and unarchive may move it back and forward, nothing else may). catalog_archive_entries are append-only like every other Catalog record, and a create guard holds each new entry to what the archive route saves (own part's revision, Change of the matching kind with the same seq, ID derived from the Change's correlation ID, a real change of state, a revision left not archived, the newest such named as current afterwards); saving the entry then moves the part's current revision there itself (e.app.save, checked by the part guard), so no server code can leave a part on an archived or older revision. catalog_csv_reviews (kicad-parts-75a5) are append-only too, and a create guard holds each review to what the review route saves: its problem is a csv-details-differ-from-edited-details or csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision problem whose subject is the review's part's IPN, code copied, csv_sha256 equal to the sha256 of the problem's recorded CSV document, a Change of kind csv-review with the same seq, the ID derived from the Change's correlation ID, and accepted a JSON list of names. A new part revision must be the part's newest number + 1 (archived or not), with the newest as predecessor and the ID derived from part and number (onRecordCreate). New catalog_part_details must be the part's newest number + 1, with the newest as predecessor and the ID derived from part and number (onRecordCreate). A new CAD item revision must be its CAD item's newest number + 1, with the newest as predecessor and the ID derived from CAD item and number (onRecordCreate). Collection drops in down migrations are not record deletes, so rollback still works. Tests that need a tampered record (ID-collision cases) stop the server, UPDATE data.db with rusqlite, and restart on the same data dir.

title: Each CSV import run records what the CSV said; the zero-loss report rebuilds the CSV from the latest run
rationale: A CSV import run's audit entry (catalog_audit_entries: csv_file, csv_import_number from 1 without gaps, source_commit, allowed_older_checkout, file_hashes, sources) records the files read with byte hashes, each CSV file's header line and every row's bytes, the current revision and details it left each part at (parts: [{ipn, revision, details}]), the parts earlier runs made that no row makes now (removed_parts), and the IDs of every import problem it found (new or already stored), whether or not it makes a Change. Every run sends exactly one catalog-csv source (database/<csvFile>.csv) and one substitutes-csv source; the route checks sha256(header + rows) against the file hash, refuses empty rows, and checks that every part's source row is one of those rows. A run is recorded (200 nothing_changed) whenever it read other files than the previous run of the same CSV file, even with no revision or problem, so the latest run always holds what the CSV says now; 422 noop only when nothing is new and the files are the same. A part an earlier run made that no row makes now gets a part-not-in-csv-file import problem whose detail does not name a run, so every later run finds it again; nothing is deleted. tooling/catalog-import zero_loss.rs rebuilds the CSV from the latest run (checking the recorded row count against the parsed rows, and file_hashes against the recorded files), matches rows by IPN (row problems by row number plus exact row bytes), accepts only import problems the latest run found (problems are shared by content, so an earlier run's problem must never explain a row) and none for two rows, compares each row's Symbol and Footprint with the revision, and every other details column with the part details, that run left the part at (so later edits do not matter; a kind kept by csv-details-differ-from-edited-details or csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision is accounted as an import problem), reads supplier data from the run's rows, and matches incomplete-main-manufacturer-part problems by the row's own MPN and Manufacturer. A symbol keeps its revision when a neighbouring symbol in its library changes, so its stored source may name an older file hash and byte range: the report checks the blob against the whole symbol in the current file, and when the source names the current file it also checks the stored range. It checks 3D model references on the footprint revision the parts actually bind. Current revision sources are never used by the report.

title: CSV imports carry the current revision they expect per part; the importer refuses an older checkout and uncommitted changes
rationale: ImportCommand carries the current revision and current details it expects per part (parts[].expectedRevision and parts[].expectedDetails, 0 for a part expected to be new; kicad-parts-7556) and per CAD item (cadItemRevisions[].expectedRevision, read by read_import_state; a moved CAD item is a 409 conflict listed in cadItemConflicts) and the latest import run of its CSV file it read (expectedCsvImport, 0 if none); both are set only by ImportCommand::expecting(read_import_state), the older-checkout setting only by allowing_older_checkout and the uncommitted-changes setting only by allowing_uncommitted_changes. These fields are private because each setter derives the correlation ID again from the import fingerprint plus all of them, so re-running the same import after it applied gets a fresh comparison (422 noop) and re-sending an identical command replays. The same import with a different reason still gets 409 correlation_reused, as any reused ID for a different request does. If another import of the file landed in between, POST /api/catalog/csv-imports answers 409 newer_import_run; if any part's current revision or details differ, 409 conflict listing every such part with its current revision and details (the message names at most 10). Both write nothing and are not stored, like edit conflicts. read_import_state downloads only the latest run of each CSV file, and only its small fields (id, csv_file, csv_import_number, source_commit; kicad-parts-7828, mx-e06414). Uncommitted changes (kicad-parts-7348, decision mx-08bf3f): the planner keeps the paths it read (sources) and the paths it looked for but did not find (CsvImport::missing_inputs: a symbol library, the first footprint choice's .kicad_mod, a 3D model candidate). services::plan compares them with HEAD (compare_with_head): a read file whose bytes differ from HEAD's blob (git --literal-pathspecs ls-tree -r -z HEAD against git hash-object --no-filters, at most 100 paths per run) or that HEAD lacks, or a missing file that HEAD has (deleted, or renamed even only in letter case), makes the source commit HEAD+dirty. Comparing bytes, not git status, also catches case-only renames on Windows and skip-worktree/assume-unchanged files; the inputs are -text, so equal bytes hash equally. A folder that is not the repository's top folder (git rev-parse --show-toplevel, compared after canonicalize), such as a copy inside an ignored target/, has no source commit. services::prepare_import(client, repository, import, reason, Allow { older_checkout, uncommitted_changes }) first calls services::check_committed, before any request: a +dirty import is refused unless Allow.uncommitted_changes, with a reason naming the changed files (services::uncommitted_files, at most 10), telling the person to commit first or use --allow-uncommitted-changes, and warning: "Until you commit these changes and import again, a later import from a checkout without them will undo them." Only the files the import reads or looks for count, so other work in the checkout never blocks. The route accepts csvFile only as a plain name (^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$, kicad-parts-7828, mx-e06414) and sourceCommit only empty or ^[0-9a-f]{40}(\+dirty)?$ (400 otherwise), refuses +dirty unless allowUncommittedChanges is true, refuses allowUncommittedChanges without +dirty ("there are no uncommitted changes to allow"), and records the setting as allowed_uncommitted_changes on the run's audit entry (migration 1792100000_uncommitted_changes.js; its undo refuses while any run has it true). After a +dirty run of a CSV file, a run from a clean commit is recorded even with the same files and nothing new (nothing_changed instead of 422 noop), so committing the changes and importing again makes the latest run name that commit and the older-checkout check protects it. prepare_import sends the setting only when it is used. catalog-import pilot takes --allow-uncommitted-changes; local-team-server, and tests that import from this checkout, allow uncommitted changes themselves, because their server is thrown away. Older checkout: the server cannot run git, so tooling/catalog-import checkout.rs (used by prepare_import) checks the latest import run of every CSV file: the import's commit must be that run's commit or a descendant (git merge-base --is-ancestor). A +dirty commit counts as its base commit on both sides. The earlier per-file tracking of uncommitted runs (file hashes and git diff between commits) was removed in 7348: an uncommitted run now needs the explicit override, whose message warns that until the changes are committed and imported again a later import from a checkout without them undoes them, like an older checkout. services::read_source_commit tells a missing git apart from a folder outside git, so the check says plainly when git is not installed. A commit the checkout lacks, files not read from git and recorded commits that are not 40 hex digits are refused too, one line per commit. allow_older_checkout skips the check and is recorded as allowed_older_checkout on the run's audit entry. Tests: catalog-import services (a_changed_new_or_deleted_input_is_recorded_as_dirty, a_change_git_is_told_to_ignore_still_counts, a_folder_that_is_not_the_top_of_a_repository_has_no_commit, uncommitted_changes_are_refused_before_anything_is_sent, a_deleted_or_renamed_footprint_is_an_uncommitted_change, only_changes_to_the_files_an_import_uses_count), checkout unit tests, pocketbase_reimports an_older_checkout_is_refused_unless_allowed_and_the_override_is_recorded (override, commit, recorded nothing_changed run, sibling refused), pocketbase_import (route refusals incl. malformed source commits and nothing to allow; an_import_allowed_from_uncommitted_changes_is_recorded_kept_and_not_undone).

name: Blob hashing in the CSV import route: UTF-8 text through PocketBase, other bytes through JavaScript
description: $security.sha256 hashes text only. A blob whose bytes are UTF-8 (every real CAD file so far) is sent as text (blobs[].text) and the route hashes it with $security.sha256(text) and stores toBytes(text): both turn the same JS string into the same UTF-8 bytes, so the stored bytes are exactly the hashed ones (about 50 ms per MiB; invalid UTF-8 or lone surrogates become U+FFFD on both sides, so a false hash claim is refused). Other bytes are sent as base64 and decoded and hashed in pure JS (catalog_lib.js, about 3 s per MiB; the 60 s client timeout would fail near 20 MiB). Exactly one of text/base64 per blob. Passing a Go []byte or a JS array to $security.sha256 does NOT hash the bytes: goja stringifies it as '72,69,...'. The route sets $apis.bodyLimit(32 MiB) (PocketBase's default; above it PocketBase answers 413 or resets the connection while the client still sends), and submit_import serializes the body once and refuses one over IMPORT_BODY_LIMIT before sending. Measured on the real catalog: g-con (largest model, 1.5 MiB) 5.4 s -> 0.17 s; the 7 CSV files using all 13 models 14.4 s -> 0.67 s; largest request g-con at 1,900,969 bytes (1.8 MiB). An empty 3D model file is an empty-3d-model-reference import problem (file kept as a source), never a blob; the route still refuses empty blobs. Tests: tooling/catalog-import tests the_route_hashes_blob_bytes_exactly (both forms) and pocketbase_categories every_real_3d_model_imports_in_one_request_per_csv_file.

name: Catalog hook storage and shared code
description: Kept from mx-be5c16: canonical documents whose SHA-256 is their identity (revision snapshots) are stored in text fields with an explicit max (a TextField max of 0 means 5000), never json fields, so the hashed bytes round-trip. Shared hook code lives in a non-.pb.js file loaded with require(`${__hooks}/catalog_lib.js`) inside the handler; values used when registering a route (such as $apis.bodyLimit's limit) may be top-level consts of the .pb.js file.

title: Extra MPN columns, MPN TBC and unknown MPN columns become import problems; Excluded from BOM comes only from KiCad's own BOM flags
rationale: route_column: 'MPN' followed by digits (g-rfm MPN2) is ExtraMpn, 'MPN TBC' (g-rvr) is MpnToBeConfirmed, and any other header containing 'mpn' in any case ('MPN 2', 'Alt MPN', 'mpn2') is UnknownMpn; none goes into the part details. A non-blank MPN2 is an mpn-without-manufacturer import problem (detail: column, mpn, row_manufacturer) because a manufacturer part needs a manufacturer and nothing in the CSV says the row's Manufacturer makes it (Wurth 3670128 vs MS128-10F). MPN TBC is an mpn-to-be-confirmed import problem (detail: column, value): unconfirmed MPNs are not approved manufacturer parts. UnknownMpn values are unknown-mpn-column import problems (detail: column, value); no real CSV has one. Blank cells add nothing. PartRevision.excluded_from_bom (part of the revision since kicad-parts-7556; serde default, written only when true, last field; since kicad-parts-ccc0 the server works it out again from the bound CAD's stored bytes for every new revision, by import, edit or CSV review, and refuses an import that claims otherwise; nobody can set it by hand and an existing revision never changes) is true when a local symbol the part binds says (in_bom no), or every footprint choice is a local footprint with exclude_from_bom in its (attr ...). If only some footprint choices are marked (an unread KiCad-library choice counts as not marked) and the symbol is not, it stays unset and a footprint-choices-disagree-on-bom import problem keeps the choices. Notes and descriptions are never read. In the CSV catalog it is set for ART-0000-0001 only (g-art:TestPoint). ART-0001-0006 has no evidence either way: its symbol g-con:Conn_PIC_TagConnect_TC2030 is missing (missing-member) and its footprint is in KiCad's bundled library, which is not read. The g-no_bom libraries are all marked but unused. The zero-loss report checks all these rules (column table in zero_loss.rs, tests every_column_of_every_csv_file_has_one_destination and the_zero_loss_report_fails_when_its_new_checks_find_a_loss) and all 21 CSV files pass the pilot.

title: Edits made in the app always win over CSV imports; differences are accepted field by field
rationale: User decision, 2026-10-10. A re-import never overwrites what an edit saved. Since kicad-parts-7556 this holds per part and per kind: a part's details follow the CSV only while its current details came from a CSV import, and its CAD only while its current revision did; otherwise csv-details-differ-from-edited-details or csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision keeps the row (catalog_csv_imports.pb.js). So a description edited in the app stays while a CSV footprint change still adds a revision. Since kicad-parts-75a5 the desktop app shows a notice on such a part, but only when the CSV changed after the edit (not for an import of the unchanged CSV); the person reviews each field where the CSV differs and ticks which CSV values to accept. That saves a Change of kind csv-review (details: next details, no revision; Symbol or Footprint: a new revision), never a normal edit, built by the server from the recorded CSV values. Unpicked fields stay as they are, and keeping all current values is recorded too. A review covers what the CSV said, so it asks again only when the CSV changes (see the CSV review pattern).

title: Number CAD item revisions like parts; KiCad always gets the current revision
rationale: User decision on 9e05, 2026-10-10 (option 1). Going back to earlier content adds a new numbered CAD item revision, while the bytes stay stored once, so a CAD item's current revision is always its newest. KiCad has no revision concept (database libraries refer to Library:Name); how KiCad gets revisions is now mx-f75a28. Built in kicad-parts-54d5: a CAD item revision ID is deriveId('cad-item-revision', cad_item + newline + number); part revisions (part details before kicad-parts-7556) and footprint snapshots name a revision by cad_item, number and snapshot_sha256. A binding (a part's symbol or footprint, or a footprint's 3D model) keeps the revision it names while its CAD content is the same, because the same content under a newer number is not a change (mx-5e5fb1). Only a change of CAD content, or a Symbol or Footprint field naming another CAD item, moves a binding, and then it names the CAD item's current revision. So parts the imports keep follow A, B, A to revisions 1, 2 and 3, while a part that missed B (its CAD kept by an edit, or in another CSV file) stays on revision 1 with no new revision and no import problem. Edits never renumber a binding (restores, which copied an older revision exactly, were removed in kicad-parts-9296). Parts do not always bind a CAD item's current number. How it works: the pattern 'CAD item revisions are numbered; snapshots name them by number and hash' (mx-0a590f).

title: Imports from uncommitted changes are refused unless overridden
rationale: User decision on 7348, 2026-10-10: commit first, because one simple rule is easier to explain than tracking uncommitted changes across later imports. Built in kicad-parts-7348: an import whose files differ from HEAD (+dirty: a read file changed or new, or a file it looked for deleted or renamed) is refused before anything is sent, naming the changed files, unless --allow-uncommitted-changes (Allow.uncommitted_changes) is given; only the files the import reads or looks for count. The server accepts only an empty or 40-hex(+dirty) source commit, refuses +dirty without allowUncommittedChanges and the setting without +dirty (400), and records it as allowed_uncommitted_changes on the run's audit entry. The tracking of uncommitted runs across later imports was removed: a +dirty run counts as its commit. To make the override's warning true, a clean run after a +dirty run of the same CSV file is always recorded (nothing_changed), so 'until you commit these changes and import again, a later import from a checkout without them will undo them'. The local team server allows uncommitted changes itself, since its data is thrown away. Details in mx-64c42a.

title: A revision is a CAD change; part details and manufacturer parts are shared; archive instead of restore
rationale: User decision, 2026-10-10. Old products must keep the exact parts they were designed with while new designs use the newest. A part revision is the exact symbol, footprint and 3D model revisions a part uses, and only a CAD change adds one; the same CAD content under a newer CAD item number is not a change. Part details (description, value, datasheet) and manufacturer parts belong to the IPN and every revision shares them: changing them is recorded in the history but adds no revision. A part that can no longer replace the old one gets a new IPN. Restore goes away: a bad revision is archived (hidden from KiCad and the app, still found by designs that use it, never deleted), and the current revision is the newest one not archived. The IPN never carries the revision. Built in kicad-parts-7556 (shared part details, revisions as CAD only; see the pattern 'Part details are stored apart from part revisions') after kicad-parts-9296 removed Restore; archive was built in kicad-parts-5bea (see the pattern 'Archived part revisions').

name: CAD item revisions are numbered; snapshots name them by number and hash
description: Seed kicad-parts-54d5. IDs: a CAD item revision is deriveId('cad-item-revision', cad_item + newline + number) (crates/catalog ids.rs CadItemRevisionId::new, catalog_lib.js); blobs stay content-derived, so revisions with the same bytes share one blob. A CAD item's current revision is its newest number (no pointer field); a create guard in catalog_write_guards.pb.js refuses a new CAD item revision that is not newest+1 with the newest as predecessor and the derived ID. References: CadReferenceTarget and ModelTarget::CadItemRevision are {cad_item, number, snapshot_sha256}; the number gives the record ID, the hash lets readers (desktop checked_snapshot, zero-loss report) check the record. Same content: CadItemDetails::content_sha256 (and contentOf in catalog_csv_imports.pb.js, over key-sorted canonicalJson so key order cannot hide equal content) hashes a snapshot with its 3D model binding numbers set to 0, so a footprint naming model revision 3 has the same content as one naming model revision 1 when those models have the same content. Keeping: a binding keeps the revision it names while its content hash equals the CAD item's current revision's; otherwise it names the current revision. Import: CsvCatalog::import numbers as if the catalog were empty; ImportCommand::expecting calls CsvImport::numbered_against(read_import_state's current_cad: each CAD item's current revision with a footprint's model bindings, and each part's current bindings, from its current part revision's cad_item_revisions relation; only current records and the older revisions those parts bind are read, mx-e06414), 3D models first. Each cadItemRevisions entry carries expectedRevision (current number read, 0 if new), number (expected if content equals the current revision's snapshot, else expected+1) and the derived id. The route refuses a wrong id or number (400), a second entry for one CAD item (400), a binding with keys other than kind/cad_item/number/snapshot_sha256 (400), a new CAD item revision whose content equals the current revision's and differs only in the numbers it names (400), a binding that does not keep exactly the revision the part's (or footprint's) stored current revision binds while that has the same content as the CAD item's current revision after the request (400, so the server requires keeping, not just allows it), and any other binding that is not that current revision (400); 409 conflict with cadItemConflicts [{kind,key,expectedRevision,currentRevision}] when a CAD item moved since it was read. A stored current revision whose ID, number or snapshot hash is inconsistent is an id_collision. A part whose current revision an edit saved, and whose CAD content really differs in the row, gets csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision ('the symbols, footprints or 3D models that the row of X uses differ from its current revision N, which was saved by an edit'; kicad-parts-7556). Edits keep a binding the current revision already has exactly; a newly named reference binds the current revision. (Restores, which copied the stored bytes, were removed in kicad-parts-9296.) The zero-loss report compares the parts' bindings of one reference by content hash and checks every bound revision. Migration 1791700000_cad_item_revision_numbers.js drops the unique (cad_item, snapshot_sha256) index (adds a plain one) and refuses to start, changing nothing, on data whose CAD item revision IDs are not number-derived; its undo refuses whenever any CAD item revision exists. Tests: crates/catalog csv_import going_back_to_earlier_cad_content_is_numbered_as_a_new_revision; tooling/catalog-import pocketbase_reimports going_back_to_earlier_cad_content_adds_a_revision_that_parts_bind, pocketbase_import (forged ids/numbers, stale CAD items, old data and undo refused), pocketbase_edits server_code_cannot_move_a_part_backwards_or_skip_a_revision, desktop_team_previews after_going_back_to_earlier_content_previews_draw_each_revisions_own_cad.

title: Archive rules: never the last revision, undo with a reason, part revisions only; per-part ownership of details and CAD
rationale: User decisions, 2026-10-10 (bd76 plan, all recommendations approved). The last revision of a part that is not archived cannot be archived (add a corrected revision first), so every part always has a current revision. Archiving can be undone (Unarchive) with a reason, by the same people who can archive. Only part revisions are archived for now; CAD item revisions keep current = newest. App edits win over CSV imports per part and per kind: a part follows CSV details only while its latest saved details came from an import, and CSV CAD only while its current revision came from an import; otherwise the difference is an import problem to accept field by field (kicad-parts-75a5). Excluded from BOM is recalculated from the CAD of every new revision and shown read-only (kicad-parts-ccc0). The app may edit Value and change Symbol and Footprint, with the hint that a part with a different value, package or pinout needs a new IPN. Sim_* columns are shared part details. Not built yet (kicad-parts-bd76 steps).

name: Part details are stored apart from part revisions
description: Seed kicad-parts-7556 (decision mx-5e5fb1). Two kinds of immutable, numbered, hashed records per part. catalog_part_details (migration 1791800000_shared_part_details.js): part, number from 1 per part, predecessor, change, snapshot (PartDetails schema kicad-parts/part-details/2: ipn, fields, manufacturer_parts; never Symbol or Footprint), snapshot_sha256, source; ID deriveId('part-details', part + newline + number). catalog_part_revisions keep their collection, but the snapshot is PartRevision schema kicad-parts/part-revision/1: ipn, cad_fields (Symbol and Footprint exactly as written), cad_references, excluded_from_bom. catalog_parts gains current_details and current_details_number; guards let the details pointer move only to the next details, the revision pointer only to the newest revision that is not archived (kicad-parts-5bea), and new part details and part revisions must be newest+1 with the derived ID. Both routes check what each document holds (catalog_lib.js detailsProblem and revisionProblem): details may not list Symbol or Footprint, a revision's cad_fields are only Symbol then Footprint, each at most once, every field and manufacturer part is a pair of text values, and cad_references must be exactly the references the cad_fields name (split on ;, trimmed like Rust, in order); otherwise 400 and nothing written. Change kinds are csv-import, edit, archive, unarchive and csv-review (kicad-parts-75a5); a Change holds at least one part revision, CAD item revision, saved part details, archive entry or CSV review. Edits (POST /api/catalog/edits, catalog_lib.js publishEdit): { correlationId, reason, ipn, details?: { expectedDetails, fields, manufacturerParts }, cad?: { expectedRevision, fields } }, each section sent only when it changed (catalog-browser compares with the details and revision the person started from), each checked against its own number, so a details edit never conflicts with a CAD change; 409 gives currentDetails and/or currentRevision for what moved; applied gives details and/or revision. CSV imports: route_column sends Symbol and Footprint to ColumnRoute::Cad; parts[] carry expectedRevision, expectedDetails, details { snapshot, snapshotSha256 }, revision { snapshot, snapshotSha256 } and one source. Ownership is per part and per kind: changed details are saved only if the current details' Change kind is csv-import, else csv-details-differ-from-edited-details; changed CAD adds a revision only if the current revision's is, else csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision. When both are unchanged the row is compared with the source of whichever current record was saved later: part-last-saved-without-csv-source if that was an edit, csv-row-changed-without-part-details-change if only supplier data changed. Runs record parts as {ipn, revision, details}; Counts add partDetails and updatedDetails. The replica holds each part's current revision and current details (a Change may hold only details); the desktop history has one entry per Change (HistoryEntry with revision and/or details). The migration refuses old data (any part revision) with a plain start-fresh message; its undo refuses any saved part details, so a full rollback works only on a catalog without parts.

name: Archived part revisions
description: Seed kicad-parts-5bea (decision mx-5e5fb1). A bad part revision is archived, never deleted or changed: migration 1791900000_archived_revisions.js adds catalog_archive_entries (part, part_revision, revision_number, archived bool, change, seq = the Change's seq, current_revision_after, current_revision_number_after; ID deriveId('archive-entry', correlation ID)) and the Change kinds archive and unarchive; one entry per Change (unique index on change); its undo refuses any archive entry. A create guard holds every entry to what the route saves: its part_revision is that part's revision with that number, its Change has the matching kind (archive/unarchive) and the same seq, its ID is deriveId('archive-entry', the Change's correlation ID), it really changes the state, it leaves a revision not archived, and current_revision_after names the newest such revision; saving the entry moves the part's current revision there (the route no longer saves the part itself). A revision's state is its newest entry by seq (catalog_lib.js archiveState; Rust archived_numbers / CatalogReadback::archived). The part's current revision is its newest revision not archived (newestNotArchived), and the part-update guard requires exactly that. POST /api/catalog/archives { correlationId, reason, ipn, revision, archived } (catalog_archives.pb.js, publishArchive): can_edit_catalog members and superusers, reason required; 404 for a missing revision; 422 noop when the state is already that; 400 'Revision N is the only revision that is not archived, so it cannot be archived. Add a corrected revision first.' when archiving would leave none; otherwise one Change, one archive entry, the part's pointer move (if any) and one audit entry (catalog.archive / catalog.unarchive). Unarchive is allowed with a reason. Only part revisions are archived; CAD item revisions keep current = newest. New revisions (edits and imports) are numbered after the newest revision, archived or not, with it as predecessor (part-revision create guard). An import never brings an archived design back: CAD whose server-side content (partRevisionContent: the revision with every binding replaced by its CAD item revision's cadContent) equals an archived revision's records csv-cad-matches-archived-revision on every run and adds nothing; a CAD edit that really changes the CAD to such content gets 400 'unarchive revision N instead' (an unchanged CAD section sent with a details edit never does). The replica applies archive-only Changes through ChangeRecords::fetch (made_current holds the revisions the entries point to); if one cannot be fetched, fetch fails and apply returns a gap, so the follower catches up instead of guessing. The desktop history has archive entries (HistoryEntry.archive), TeamPart.revisions lists each revision's state, and PublishResult::Archived reports the new current revision. The zero-loss report accepts csv-cad-matches-archived-revision for a row's CAD columns and checks that every part's current revision is its newest not archived.

name: Reviewing CSV changes on edited parts
description: Seed kicad-parts-75a5 (decision mx-ee29d9). When an import keeps a row in csv-details-differ-from-edited-details or csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision, a person reviews it field by field. POST /api/catalog/csv-reviews (catalog_csv_reviews.pb.js, catalog_lib.js publishCsvReview) takes { correlationId, reason, ipn, problem, accept: [field names], expected } and nothing else: the server builds what it saves from the problem's recorded CSV document (detail.details or detail.revision), so values sent by a client are ignored. Details problems accept details field names and 'Manufacturer parts' (the whole list); CAD problems accept 'Symbol' and 'Footprint' (field value and that role's cad_references, each CSV cad-item-revision checked to be stored with the recorded snapshot_sha256). A field not in both, or equal to the part's, is 400. expected is the current details number (details) or current revision number (CAD); a mismatch is 409 conflict with currentDetails/currentRevision. The part may have been edited since the import: the CSV values are compared with what the part has now. The problem must be in the latest import run of its CSV file (csv file from problem.path database/<f>.csv, audit entry sources.problems), else 409 out_of_date. Taking details saves details number+1 (no revision); taking CAD adds revision newest+1, refused with the edit message 'unarchive revision N instead' when the CAD matches an archived revision; an empty accept keeps the current values. Every review is one Change of kind csv-review (migration 1792000000_csv_reviews.js) with one catalog_csv_reviews record (part, problem, code, csv_sha256 = sha256 of the recorded CSV document, accepted JSON list, change, seq; ID deriveId('csv-review', correlation ID); unique (part, code, csv_sha256) and (change)) and an audit entry catalog.csv-review; a second review of the same CSV values is 422 noop. Resolve, not narrow: one review answers the whole problem, unpicked fields are deliberately kept, and later imports still record the problem (the zero-loss report needs it) but the review covers it by (part, code, csv_sha256); new CSV values make a new snapshot, so the notice returns. Edge: CSV values going A to B and back to A stay covered for A. Edits in the app alone never bring the notice back, because the CSV did not change. Decision (coordinator, best judgement for the user, step 4 reviews): the app asks only when the CSV changed since it was last applied or reviewed. For each kind, catalog-browser takes the newer by Change seq of (a) the snapshot of the newest details (details problem) or revision (CAD problem) a csv-import Change saved and (b) the csv_sha256 of the newest review of that part and kind, whose document comes from the reviewed problem; a problem whose recorded CSV document has that SHA-256 is left out. Any review whose (code, csv_sha256) matches still covers a problem, agreeing with the server's 422 noop. So an edit followed by an import of the unchanged CSV shows nothing, while a CSV that changes back to an earlier text after values were accepted asks again. The problem is still recorded for the zero-loss report. Every differing field is listed; CsvChangeRow.changed_in_csv is false when the comparison document has the same value (the part was edited away from it, so accepting undoes the edit), those rows come last and show '(not changed in the CSV)', and nothing is pre-ticked. The desktop computes TeamPart.csv_changes in catalog-browser (problems_of, csv_reviews_of, latest_import_run with perPage=1; open = in the latest run, not covered by a review, not equal to the last imported document, rows not empty; a recorded document that does not parse is skipped so the part still opens) and the follower also subscribes to catalog_audit_entries: a run with csv_import_number > 0, and every catch-up, bumps TeamSession::SignedIn.imports, which the UI's team_checkpoint memo includes, because a run that only finds problems publishes no Change. The local team server takes 'reimport' or 'reimport <folder>' lines on stdin (--json) for journeys, and 'reimport' typed in the console otherwise. The UI sends one request per open group (details, then CAD), built at click time from ui.reviewing; a group whose review is saved, or gets 422 (already reviewed), leaves ui.reviewing and the form's rows at once, so a retry sends only the groups still open; a refusal after an earlier save says "Your choice for the part details was saved. Your choice for the symbol and footprint was not: <message>". When open values disappear from the part, the form closes saying either a newer import found different CSV values (values of that kind are still open) or (none of that kind left) 'These CSV values are no longer open, so nothing was saved.' out_of_date reads "A newer import has run since you opened these CSV values. Nothing was saved. Open the part again to see what differs now." (only administrators import). Without --desktop the console stops only on Enter alone; other text gets a reminder.

name: Excluded from BOM is worked out by the server for every new revision
description: Seed kicad-parts-ccc0 (decision mx-9a51aa, plan pl-e6a8 step 5). Excluded from BOM belongs to the part revision and comes only from KiCad's flags in the bytes of the CAD item revisions it binds: a symbol entry with (in_bom no) (any top-level symbol in the symbol blob, as the zero-loss report reads it), or every footprint choice whose .kicad_mod has exclude_from_bom in an (attr ...). A reference not bound to a stored CAD item revision (KiCad's own library such as Device:R, or a missing symbol or footprint) gives no evidence; kicad-parts-76c3 reads KiCad's libraries later. catalog_lib.js has a small s-expression reader (sexpTokens, sexpChildren, symbolSaysNotInBom, footprintExcludedFromBom) that must match crates/kicad-integration library_file.rs byte for byte: bytes become text one character per byte (bytesText, String.fromCharCode in chunks; never toString, which decodes UTF-8), only ASCII space, tab, LF, FF and CR separate tokens (not \s, which also matches VT, NBSP, U+FEFF, U+2028), and any unnamed top-level symbol entry makes the symbol bytes unreadable (false), as SymbolLibrary::parse fails. The shared Rust readers are kicad_integration::library_file::{symbol_entries_say_not_in_bom, footprint_says_excluded_from_bom}, used by the zero-loss report and catalog-browser; pocketbase_bom.rs has a parity test that sends crafted bytes to a test hook calling lib.bomMark and compares. excludedFromBom(document, markOf) takes markOf(target, role) -> true/false/null. Stored bytes are read in the JSVM with $app.newFilesystem().getReader(blob.baseFilesPath() + '/' + blob.getString('file')) and toBytes(reader), closing both (blobBytes); storedBomMarks reads only a CAD item revision whose snapshot kind is the bound role and judges each blob once. The edit route's cad section and the CSV review route set the new revision's value from it (they no longer copy the old value); the import route refuses with 400 a part revision whose value differs from what the server reads, taking bytes from the request's blobs (toBytes of the text, or the decoded base64) for CAD item revisions it sends, else as stored, judging each blob once; it also refuses a symbol or footprint reference whose target is not deriveId('cad-item', role + newline + reference), as edits and the zero-loss report require. An existing revision never changes: old designs keep the revision they use, so a new revision never changes another project's BOM. footprint-choices-disagree-on-bom stays an import problem the Rust importer records; an edit to disagreeing choices just leaves it unset. The zero-loss report checks every stored part revision (bom_marks, check_every_revision_excluded_from_bom) besides the latest run's rows. The desktop shows CurrentRevision.excluded_from_bom words in the Symbol and footprint table: 'Yes: its symbol says it is not in the BOM', 'Yes: every footprint choice says it is not in the BOM', 'No', 'No: only some footprint choices say it is not in the BOM', or 'Not known: the symbol comes from KiCad's own library, which this app does not read yet' / '... is not in the Catalog' / '... could not be read', only when an unread symbol, or unread footprint choices with no known choice in the BOM, could change the answer. catalog-browser bom_marks infers most marks from the revision's own setting (not excluded: no stored symbol says so, nor a single stored footprint) and reads stored bytes only for an excluded revision's symbols and for several footprint choices. The history's Excluded from BOM row says 'Yes'/'No'. The zero-loss report names a revision whose snapshot does not parse. Tests: tooling/catalog-import/tests/pocketbase_bom.rs, desktop_team.rs, catalog-browser unit test, journey 06.

name: The import state reads only current records
description: Seed kicad-parts-7828. read_import_state (crates/catalog/src/pocketbase.rs) reads, with fields= so no rows or bytes: every catalog_parts record (small fields: current revision and details numbers); each CAD item's current revision with filter catalog_cad_item_revisions_via_predecessor.id = "" (the newest is the one no revision names as its predecessor; the create guard keeps the predecessor chain); each part's current revision with filter part.current_revision = id (fields part,cad_item_revisions); the bound CAD item revisions that are not current, by ID through id_filters (40 IDs per request); and the latest import run of each CSV file (read_latest_imports: first_record_fields with filter csv_import_number > 0 && csv_file > <the file found last>, sorted csv_file,-csv_import_number, so the CSV files in name order, one small request per file plus one that finds none, with a filter of constant length). The import route takes csvFile only as ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$ (400 otherwise), because PocketBase filters undo only \" escapes: a backslash, tab or newline in a name would break the read for every CSV file. A footprint's snapshot names its 3D model revisions, so they need no read. The importer never needs archived revisions' content: the server checks that an import never brings an archived design back. PocketBase 0.38 filter notes: the back-relation filter X_via_predecessor.id = "" (or = null) works for 'has no successor'; X_via_predecessor:length = 0 is a 400. Without an index on predecessor the newest-revision filter grows about cubically and SQLite does not build a temporary index (reviewer: 0.78 s at 2,000 revisions, 19.2 s at 6,000, about 90 s at 10,000), so migration 1792200000_cad_item_revision_successor.js adds the unique partial index idx_catalog_cad_item_revisions_predecessor on (predecessor) WHERE predecessor != '' (0.19 s at 6,000). Unique also stops two revisions following the same one, which would fork a history; the migration refuses such data with a plain message and changes nothing, and its undo only drops the index. The collection guards (collectionChangeProblem) already refuse dropping any catalog index through the API. Test: pocketbase_import a_cad_item_revision_has_at_most_one_successor (a second successor written straight into SQLite fails on the index; after undoing it the fork goes in and starting refuses). The migration tests' down counts went up by one. Proof: the pilot output for all 21 CSV files and the SHA-256 of every command body (all 21 files imported twice into one server) were identical before and after. Test: tooling/catalog-import/tests/pocketbase_import_state.rs the_import_state_is_read_from_current_records_only builds history (part revisions 1-3, footprint 1-3, 3D model 1-2, an archived part revision, a part kept on footprint 1 by an edit), compares the read with the state worked out from read_back, and counts records per request through a loopback proxy that asks PocketBase to close each connection (6 requests; 29 part revisions instead of 87).

title: Guess a new part's category from layered clues the team confirms, never from the description alone
rationale: User decision 2026-10-11 (seeds kicad-parts-9693, kicad-parts-ae44), from research on Ki-nTree, inventree-part-import, Part-DB, Binner, Altium and Octopart. Real tools rarely guess well from the description alone: Ki-nTree's thefuzz fallback defaults to a threshold of 100 (exact only); Binner's weighted keyword score has no minimum and falls back to Other; Octopart's description classifier needs per-category confidence cut-offs. What works is matching clues and keeping each user choice (inventree-part-import writes the choice back as an alias; Part-DB matches alternative names). Clues, most reliable first: (1) remembered matches the team confirmed, and the same MPN already in the Catalog; (2) footprint name (KiCad R_0603*, IPC-7351 RESC*/CAPC*/INDC*), decisive for passives; (3) symbol reference letter (R, C, L, D, Q, J, Y, K; U says nothing; aliases IC=U, S=SW); (4) nearest existing parts by description, keywords, footprint and manufacturer, voting (separates chip categories); (5) later, optional: DigiKey/LCSC category via a remembered match. Show the best guess preselected with its reason, two alternatives and a search; leave it empty when no clue fires; the engineer always confirms, and confirming adds remembered matches. No AI service and no network: offline and deterministic. Downloaded ZIPs (SnapEDA, Ultra Librarian, SamacSys) carry no category and few fields, so chips land in the top three rather than first. Rules and remembered matches start from the 21 CSV categories.

title: The CSV catalog is grouped by package (footprints) and by category (team symbols)
rationale: kicad-parts-82ea, one-time regroup approved by the user (nothing in production). Footprints live in footprints/g-<KiCad 10 footprint library>.pretty, e.g. g-Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric, g-Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-23-5, g-Package_DFN_QFN, g-Diode_SMD, g-Crystal, g-TestPoint; the old g-SOT, g-qfn, g-no_bom and per-category .pretty libraries are gone. 3D models live in 3d-models/g-<footprint library>.3dshapes/<footprint name>.step and footprints reference ${GITPLM_PARTS}/3d-models/g-<lib>.3dshapes/<name>.step (KiCad's own models keep ${KICAD9_3DMODEL_DIR}). Team symbols are grouped by part category: g-pas and g-dis are split into g-res (R_US), g-cap (C), g-ind (L), g-rvr (R_Potentiometer_Trim_US), g-dio (D_Capacitance_Filled, D_RECT), g-opt (D_LED_Filled), g-trs (Q_NMOS_GSD, Q_NPN); g-no_bom symbols moved to g-art, its TestPoint renamed TestPoint_Pad_D1.0mm because g-art already had a TestPoint. Tests that used g-pas:R_US now use g-res:R_US; the example CAD item ID in ids.rs is now derived from g-Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric. parts.sqlite is rebuilt from the CSVs as one TEXT table per CSV, rows in file order, short rows padded with empty strings (this reproduces the earlier frozen copy exactly). The full old-to-new mapping is in the commit message of the regroup commit. Four g-mpu.csv footprints that are not in the repository were moved by name only: SODIMM sockets to g-Connector_PCBEdge, MirrMez699_mirrored to g-Connector_Molex.

title: CSV-sourced CAD is kept and flagged; app edits are strict about what they change
rationale: QA review 2026-10-12. A CSV row whose Symbol names several symbols, or whose Footprint lists a choice twice, imports like a missing symbol: the revision keeps the CAD exactly as the CSV says and a several-symbols or repeated-footprint-choice import problem says what to fix (the zero-loss report requires it). The edit route refuses to make either, but only when the edit changes that Symbol or Footprint value from the stored revision, so an old CSV slip never blocks an unrelated CAD edit (catalog_lib.js cadReferences). A CSV review may still accept such CAD, as the import does.

name: Edits that upload CAD files
description: Seed kicad-parts-3b8b. POST /api/catalog/edits cad.uploads: [{role symbol|footprint|3d-model, reference, fileName, formatVersion (symbols only, digits), text|base64}] (catalog_lib.js editUploads, preparedUploads). Symbols and footprints must be text (KiCad saves UTF-8); 3D models may be base64. The server reads every file itself with the same s-expression reader as the BOM marks (sexpTokens/sexpChildren on bytesText): a symbol is exactly one (symbol "NAME" ...) list alone (first byte '(' and last ')', like the import's entry span), no (extends ...), NAME = the reference's name; a footprint is a whole .kicad_mod whose (footprint|module "NAME") matches; its (model ...) paths are read with a port of library_file.rs model_references and classified with a port of csv_import classify_model_reference (catalog_lib.js modelReferences, classifyModelReference): a candidate under 3d-models/ binds the 3D model uploaded with it, else the Catalog's own (keeping the footprint's current binding while its content is the model's current content), else unresolved 'missing'; other paths stay unresolved as in the import. Snapshots are built in Rust CadItemDetails key order, so re-uploading the file the import read has the content of revision 1 (test a_footprint_file_adds_a_revision_and_other_parts_keep_theirs proves byte parity for footprints and symbols). Content equal to the CAD item's current revision adds nothing (binding keeps a same-content older number, else current); other content is current+1 (or 1 for a new CAD item); blobs and CAD items are reused by ID. Refused (400, nothing written): unknown role, two files for one kind+reference, wrong name, bad s-expression, two symbols in one file, extends, non-g library, symbol without version, empty, symbol/footprint not text, a symbol/footprint upload no field names, a 3D model no uploaded footprint names. Uploading needs edit rights (403). New CAD item revisions are saved after the Change and before the part revision, source {schema, source:'edit', file_name}, license unknown-needs-review. Applied answers add newCadItemRevisions [{kind,key,number,id,otherParts}] where otherParts counts other parts whose current revision binds that symbol/footprint (filter part.current_revision = id && part != X && cad_item_revisions.cad_item ?= Y). The route has $apis.bodyLimit(32 MiB) and submit_edit refuses a bigger body before sending (EDIT_BODY_LIMIT). crates/catalog cad_file reads chosen files into CadUploads (symbol_upload takes the entry span and library version, as the planner does) and suggests footprint libraries from the package name. Tests: tooling/catalog-import/tests/pocketbase_uploads.rs, desktop_team_files.rs, journey 10.

title: A CSV import never replaces a CAD item revision made in the app; a changed CSV file for it can only be kept
rationale: Seed kicad-parts-3b8b (decision in the seed, details by best judgement). A CAD item is 'made in the app' while its current revision's Change kind is not csv-import. read_import_state lists those (one extra request: newest revisions with change.kind != csv-import, plus one per such item for its newest csv-import revision) into CurrentCad.edited_in_app {current, last_imported}. CsvImport::numbered_against never sends such a CAD item (its blob goes too unless shared) and binds parts and footprints to the last imported revision through binding_for, so an unchanged CSV changes nothing: csv-owned parts keep their binding, and an edited part's row gets the usual csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision problem whose document equals its last imported revision, which the desktop hides. If the CSV's content differs from the last imported revision (or there is none, or a 3D model of a footprint changed that way), every part whose row uses it gets an importer-made csv-cad-differs-from-edited-cad-item problem (location rows[IPN=X].Symbol|Footprint; detail role, reference, cad_item, kept_revision, edited_revision, path, row_number, raw_record, csv_cad_item = the planner's own snapshot JSON, numbered as if the catalog were empty, so its hash changes exactly when the CSV's files do). The import route refuses (400) a sent revision of a CAD item made in the app, and checks bindings against importBase (newest csv-import revision) instead of the current one. The CSV review route accepts the new code as a cad kind (recordedCsvDocument picks detail.csv_cad_item; the guard uses it too) but refuses taking it, because the CSV's bytes are not stored: keeping it records a csv-review that covers that csv_cad_item hash. Why not store the CSV's file as a new revision: the current revision is always the newest, so storing it would replace the app's revision for KiCad. Why per part: the CSV notice and reviews are per part. catalog-browser shows it as one Symbol/Footprint row with keep_only (no checkbox) and plain words; the zero-loss report explains rows by it (match subject, path, raw_record; one per symbol/footprint).

name: Review fixes to edits with files: name rules, caught-up CSV, batched reads
description: Seed kicad-parts-3b8b review. (1) Names from chosen files reach the filesystem (preview staging writes in/<library>.pretty/<name>.kicad_mod), so PreviewCache stored_symbol/stored_footprint refuse a LibRef that LibRef::parse would refuse or that holds a control character, and catalog-browser preview_file builds its g-file fallback through LibRef::parse. crates/catalog cad_file is_plain_name (LibRef::parse halves plus no control characters, no leading '-') checks file names and references, exactly as written; the edit route mirrors it (catalog_lib.js isPlainName, uploadReferenceProblem: one colon, no spaces around, g- followed by a name). 3D model keys must be 3d-models/g-<library>.3dshapes/<file> with plain names (isCatalogModelKey / cad_file::is_catalog_model_key); a footprint naming a model elsewhere saves it as missing; symbol formatVersion must match ^20[0-9]{6}$. (2) A CSV is unchanged for a CAD item made in the app when its content equals the last imported revision's OR the app's current revision's; bindings then name that revision; the import route accepts either candidate with the keep rule; the zero-loss report accepts a revision with source 'edit' when its bytes are the oracle's (whole file, or the symbol's span). (3) read_import_state reads the newest csv-import revision of all CAD items made in the app in chunks of 40 (one request in practice). (4) Desktop: a team_part fetch whose newest history seq is lower than the part shown (same IPN) is ignored, which fixed journey 08's 'History (6)' race; FileArea keeps chosen 3D model files still named and carries the field's earlier value in TeamFile.replaces; only the newest file preview answer is shown.

content: Uploads in Edit part (kicad-parts-3b8b) only bind a 3D model whose path is 3d-models/g-<footprint library>.3dshapes/<file>; a footprint that names a Catalog model anywhere else is saved with that model missing. This is stricter than the CSV import, which binds any local model path; every model in the CSV catalog is already under g-*.3dshapes (kicad-parts-82ea), so they agree today. If the import ever meets a model elsewhere, move it rather than loosening the upload rule.

name: Categories, a part's category and remembered matches
description: Seed kicad-parts-ae44 (decisions mx-2c0f7a, mx-544722). Migration 1792300000_categories.js adds catalog_categories (code, first_change; ID deriveId('category', code)), catalog_category_revisions (category, number from 1, predecessor, change, snapshot, snapshot_sha256, source; ID deriveId('category-revision', category + newline + number); unique (category, number) and partial unique predecessor) and catalog_category_matches (category, clue select supplier-category|footprint-family|reference-letter|manufacturer, value, part, change, seq, actor, actor_name; ID deriveId('category-match', change + newline + clue); unique (change, clue)). It refuses any stored part details ('saved before parts had a category ... cannot be upgraded'); its undo refuses categories or part details, so tests that undo older migrations first set it aside (DELETE its _migrations row on the stopped server, set_aside_migration). Category snapshot = crates/catalog CategoryDetails (schema kicad-parts/category/1: code, name, ipn_prefix, fields, rules {reference_letters, footprint_patterns, keywords}); catalog_lib.js categoryDocument rebuilds it in key order and the import refuses a non-canonical one. The CSV import sends category {id, code, snapshot, snapshotSha256} for the file (code = csv file without g-, fields = its PartDetails columns in order, name and rules from STARTING_CATEGORIES); every part's details must have that category and exactly those fields. A new category is saved as revision 1; for a stored one only the fields are taken (name, prefix, rules kept) and a revision is saved only when they differ, so a supplier-only header change changes nothing. Counts gain categories and categoryRevisions; a category revision alone makes a Change (g-mec has no rows). The planner (csv_import part_details_columns) refuses a part-details column named Category in any case, with no name, named twice, longer than 500 characters, or past 200 columns, naming the file and column; the server's categoryDocument and detailsProblem refuse a Category field too, so a CSV review's Category always means the category. Part details schema is kicad-parts/part-details/3 with category after ipn; compare_details lists Category first (codes; catalog-browser shows names); detailsProblem requires a category code. Edits send details.category; when it differs, the server reads the category's newest revision and expects the stored fields followed by the new category's missing fields (values free), and saves one remembered match per clue the part has after the edit: footprint-family of the first footprint reference (footprintFamily = crates/catalog footprint_family: name after the last colon, up to the first digit, trailing _-. and space trimmed), reference-letter from the bound symbol's own Reference property (stored blob or uploaded bytes; aliases IC=U, S=SW, X/XTAL=Y, VR/POT=RV, CN=J) and the main manufacturer; the applied answer lists them as rememberedMatches. The match create guard requires a Change of kind edit with the same seq, actor and actor name, the derived ID, and the part's details saved in that Change in the match's category with predecessor details in another; so imports, CSV reviews and supplier categories alone never make one. A CSV review may accept 'Category': the part takes the CSV's category and the CSV document's fields it lacks with their values (no remembered match). title: Category calls made by best judgement in kicad-parts-ae44
rationale: Spec 2026-10-11 left these open; simplest, plainest choice each time. (1) An import takes only the fields of a category the Catalog already has and keeps its name, prefix and rules, so editing rules in the app later is never undone by an import. (2) A category stores only its part-details fields (not IPN, MPN, Manufacturer, Symbol, Footprint or supplier columns), since those are what a part in it gets; the header is still in each import run. (3) Changing back to the first category keeps the fields the change added: nothing is ever dropped. (4) A CSV review that accepts Category takes the CSV's category with the CSV's values for the fields the part lacks, and makes no remembered match, because it takes what the CSV said rather than a person's own choice of clues. (5) Remembered matches are worked out by the server from the part, never sent by a client; the supplier-category kind exists for kicad-parts-9693 and is never made by an edit yet. (6) Names: art is 'Board features' (its parts are test points and a Tag-Connect pad, not artwork); mpu keeps 'Processors and modules'. (7) The Category choice lists categories by name and sits first in Edit part's Part details; a short hint appears only after a change ('The IPN stays the same. Fields of the new category are added below.'); the details show 'Category: <name>' under the Part details heading. (8) A field added blank by a category change gets no history row; the Category row explains it. (9) The local team server's reimport still re-imports only the resistors. name: Category guess engine and its leave-one-out accuracy on the CSV catalog
description: crates/catalog/src/guess.rs guess_category(&Clues, &[CategoryDetails], &[RememberedMatch], &[ExamplePart]) -> Vec<Guess {category, name, score, reasons}>, every category ranked (stable: equal scores keep the order given), best_guess() None when every score is 0. Integer points, each layer outweighing the next: same MPN already in the Catalog 1000; remembered match up to 150 (footprint family, supplier category), 100 (reference letter), 50 (manufacturer), times this category's matches over all matches for that value plus the existing parts with that clue (review fix: one person moving one of 29 Yageo R_ resistors to Capacitors used to make every new one a capacitor, 300 vs 178; now Capacitors gets 150 x 1/30 and a move back restores the guess); footprint pattern 100; reference letter 60 (U in no rule); description keywords 30 + 10 per extra, at most 50; the 5 closest example parts vote up to 60 together (similarity: description word Jaccard x50, same footprint name 10, same family 15, same manufacturer first word 10, MPN prefix of 4+ 10, same letter 5). Reasons are plain, e.g. 'footprint CAPC1608X90N matches CAPC*', 'footprint family SOT matches 2 parts in this category', 'people chose this category once for footprint family R', 'MPN X is already IPN in this category'. Starting rules: crates/catalog/src/category.rs STARTING_CATEGORIES. kicad-integration library_file::symbol_reference reads a symbol's own Reference. Leave one out (crates/catalog/tests/category_guess_on_the_catalog.rs, 178 parts, clues = reference letter of the symbol (blank for KiCad library symbols, which are not in the repository), first footprint name without library, MPN, manufacturer, description; a tie with the right category counts as the worse rank; asserts top-3 >= 90%): overall top-1 88.2%, top-3 98.9%. Per category top-1/top-3: ana 100/100 (3), art 100/100 (2), cap 100/100 (17), con 100/100 (3), cpd 47/100 (15, TVS diodes look like diodes), dio 100/100 (4), ics 93/100 (46), ind 100/100 (8), mcu 86/100 (7), mpu 25/75 (4; MPU-0002-0001 on a Molex mezzanine footprint guesses con), opt 100/100 (1), osc 100/100 (10), pcb 0/0 (1: no symbol, no footprint, description 'Oscillator for Broadcast FM' guesses osc), pwr 75/100 (8), reg 86/100 (14), res 100/100 (29), rfm 0/100 (1), rvr 100/100 (1), swi 100/100 (1), trs 100/100 (3). Without descriptions (for information): top-1 78.1%, top-3 90.4%. Hard: cpd, mpu, pwr, rfm and pcb. Optimism to keep in mind: some starting keywords (sodimm, tagconnect, shield, trimmer, tactile) were written with the catalog in view, and the one-part categories (opt, rfm, rvr, swi, pcb) rely on rules alone in leave one out, so new parts unlike the catalog will do worse.

title: Add part calls made by best judgement in kicad-parts-9693
rationale: Spec 2026-10-12 left these open; simplest, plainest choice each time. (1) The Add part button sits beside Search parts (only for people who can edit) and opens the form in the part panel: the download's drawings on the left, the form on the right; picking a search result or Cancel closes it. (2) Every create records remembered matches, since the person always confirms the category in the form. (3) A new Change kind create rather than reusing edit, so history says Added and the match guard can tell a new part apart. (4) The next free IPN is the highest middle number of the prefix (team and CSV catalog IPNs) + 1 with variant 0001, never a gap below it; 0001 when the prefix has none. (5) MPN matches compare without case; 'Add as a manufacturer part of it instead' is offered only when that part does not already list the same manufacturer with the MPN, and opens that part's Edit part with the row added (no new route). (6) Known footprints: the same name in the team catalog's current parts or the CSV catalog's footprint files, the same pads among the CSV catalog's footprint files (footprints made in the app are compared by name only), and KiCad's own library for the suggested group by name; using one sends no footprint or 3D model file. (7) The footprint is linked to the download's 3D model (matched by file name, else the first) by rewriting its (model) path to the Catalog's folder for its library at save time; the engineer can pick another model or none. (8) A file named like an existing Catalog CAD item with other content is refused, so a new part never changes other parts' current CAD. (9) The pin and pad check also says when they agree; the license line is always shown. (10) Symbol property spellings MP and MF, short spellings some vendors use, count as MPN and manufacturer too. (11) IPN-taken answers are not stored, so the app offers the next free IPN and a retry is checked again. (12) The reason is not prefilled, as in Edit part. (13) Example parts for the guess have no reference letter (reading each symbol would need a request per part).

name: Review fixes to Add part
description: Seed kicad-parts-9693 review. (1) kicad-integration Sexp::parse refuses nesting deeper than MAX_DEPTH 256 (a 100,000-deep hostile footprint overflowed the stack when the tree was walked or dropped); the server's JS reader is flat and bounded by the body limit. title: Making CAD by hand in KiCad stays supported; a library check finds it and bad 3D model links
rationale: User decision 2026-10-12 (seeds kicad-parts-da65, kicad-parts-37a7). Engineers may still draw symbols and footprints in KiCad's editors in our g- libraries when no download exists or to do it properly. Made by hand means in our g- libraries but not in the Catalog (the Catalog records every CAD item's origin: an import run with CSV file, row and commit, or a file chosen in the app). A library check (one Rust function for the import and the desktop) warns about items no part uses (with a near-name suggestion, e.g. g-ics.csv names TP4333 but the library has IC_TP4333), symbols whose own Footprint names nothing we or KiCad have, and checks each footprint's 3D model: our library with the footprint's name is fine; our library under another name (shared) is a soft warning; a missing file in our library, or any path outside our library (absolute, home folder, relative, other variables such as GITPLM_3DMODELS) is an error; KiCad's own models and embedded models are fine. Errors count only for footprints new or changed since the last import and stop the import before sending, like the commit-first rule; the same problems on unchanged footprints are clean-up. The user chose to leave today's CSV catalog files as they are (16 missing model files, 17 unresolved, 3 paths into a home folder, the TP4333 mismatch). Add part can then start from library items (kicad-parts-37a7).

title: Library check calls made by best judgement in kicad-parts-da65
rationale: Spec 2026-10-12 left these open; simplest, plainest choice each time. (1) 'Since the last import' is per CSV file: a footprint is new when it is not in the Catalog and a row of a CSV file imported before uses it, or changed when its bytes are neither its current nor its newest imported revision's (ImportState.cad_item_bytes). A CSV file never imported takes its footprints as they are (clean-up, 'It was like this before the first import'), so today's files import one by one into one server and local-team-server, pilot and partial servers never stop on old problems. (2) A problem on a footprint no part uses and the Catalog lacks is a warning (Worth a look, 'Fix it before a part uses this footprint'), not an error: today's 3 home-folder links and 2 GITPLM_3DMODELS links are on such footprints, and the error comes when something brings the footprint in (a CSV row of an imported file, Add part from it in kicad-parts-37a7). (3) Only errors in files the import reads or looks for stop it (like the commit-first rule); other errors are printed but do not block. No override flag: fixing a link is quick, and --allow-uncommitted-changes / older checkout do not bypass it. (4) The pilot prints the check to stderr (stdout stays the JSON summary, which gains library_check counts); local-team-server's reimport runs it and answers 'refused: ...'. (5) Similar names: one contains the other ignoring case (shorter >= 3 chars) or <= 2 edits; reported once per CSV file and reference as Worth a look, only when a similar name exists. (6) A 3D model no footprint links is Not in the Catalog yet; a model linked by a library footprint is never listed on its own. (7) Desktop: the line sits under the search box ('Library check: 1 to fix, 54 new items'; to fix and new items first, other groups counted only when both are zero), red when something is to fix; it opens the view in the part panel like Add part; choosing a part, Add part or Close closes it (focus back to the line); Clean-up is a folded details. Worked out once per (editor email, checkpoint, imports), cached in CatalogBrowser; viewers and signed-out people see nothing. (8) Add part leaves out a download's own model links that point outside our library (vendor folders such as ${KIPRJMOD}) when its 3D model is not used (label '(3D model link to the download's folder left out)'); Edit part refuses a chosen footprint whose link is outside our library or names a model neither in the Catalog nor sent, before anything is sent. The server does not enforce the rule yet. (9) Symbols naming a KiCad footprint are checked against KiCad's installed libraries only when found (desktop: discovery's share_dir; import: kicad_integration::installed_share_dir, no kicad-cli run).
